_comment: Source of truth for what is published at https://vizora.cloud/tv and
https://vizora.cloud/downloads/vizora-display.apk.
`candidate` is the artifact verified by scripts/release/verify-display-apk.mjs.
`published` is the artifact currently live (null until the first publish); it is
the baseline the next release's signing certificate, versionCode and compiled
default origins are compared against.
`published` describes what customers are running RIGHT NOW, so it is only ever
updated by promoting a candidate that has actually been published. Never edit it to
make a gate pass — for a deliberate environment move use `originTransition`.
`approval` encodes the two release gates. publish-display-apk.sh REFUSES to run
while either pair is null. Do not fill these in without the named human actually
confirming. Never put the keystore, its password, or any private key in this repo.
REJECTED / NOT PUBLISHED — superseded before release by an entitlement-enforcement fix.
Operator decision 2026-08-13, after the candidate had passed every gate. 1.3.14 was
verified and Gate-A approved; it is rejected on a defect found AFTER approval, not on
a failure of the release process. Recorded in full rather than deleted, because the
identity below is a durable statement that was true and must stay checkable:
tag v1.3.14 -> commit 4c5870f8c0ba55f7d4a1b1dd247f2e2fdeb3ecca
THE TAG AND ITS ARTIFACT ARE NOT ALTERED. The tag is not moved, the APK is not
rebuilt, and no different bytes are produced under the 1.3.14 identity. The
replacement is a NEW release identity (1.3.15 / versionCode 10145), specifically so
that the provenance discipline this release engineering established is not undermined
by the first inconvenient defect.
Reason for rejection: vizora-tv#28 and #31 — a reachable billing/entitlement
enforcement bypass. An asynchronous renderer that started before `tenant:suspended`
could commit its frame on top of the suspension holding screen and transition the
device back to playing. Two independent instances (normal playlist prepare, and the
temporary-content push), both proven deterministically. On the last item of a
non-looping playlist the first instance renders INDEFINITELY, because the illegitimate
transition out of holding also cancels the self-heal retry.
Publishing 1.3.14 would not have been a regression — the defect is present in the
live 1.3.13 too — but it would have meant knowingly shipping a discovered
enforcement bypass in a build we still controlled. Fixed in vizora-tv#29 and shipped
in 1.3.15 instead.
Gate A's approval below was reset to null when this candidate was retired. An
approval is bound to exact bytes; it cannot be inherited by a different artifact.
That refusal is the control working.
rejectedCandidates.disposition: REJECTED / NOT PUBLISHED — superseded before release by entitlement-enforcement fix

_originTransition_comment: Explicit authorisation for a DELIBERATE change of backend environment. Normally
null: a release must be compiled against the same origins as the published one.
Why this exists rather than 'just update the baseline'. published.compiledOrigins
describes the artifact that is CURRENTLY LIVE. Editing it to the new origins so the
gate goes green would falsify the record of what customers are actually running, in
order to authorise a change that has not happened yet — in the one file whose job is
to be true about production. published.compiledOrigins is therefore IMMUTABLE until
the new candidate is actually published, at which point candidate is promoted in the
normal way and this block is cleared.
Shape, when a migration is approved:
"from":       { "api": ..., "realtime": ..., "dashboard": ... },
"to":         { "api": ..., "realtime": ..., "dashboard": ... },
"approvedBy": "<name>",
"approvedAt": "YYYY-MM-DD"
The gate accepts a difference from the published baseline only when `from` matches
the live published origins exactly, `to` matches BOTH the packaged artifact and the
releaseOrigins policy pin, and an approver and date are recorded. Requiring `from`
to match the live baseline makes the authorisation self-invalidating: once the
migration is published, the same block can no longer wave through a second, different
move — it has to be re-approved against the new baseline.

_comment: The backend origins a published Vizora Display APK must be COMPILED WITH as its
defaults. All three are required: the verifier rejects a partial pin, because
comparing only the keys that happen to be present silently drops the rest.
SCOPE — read this before relying on it. This pins BUILD PROVENANCE: which origins
were compiled into the artifact. It is NOT a statement about where a running
device ends up pointed. The client seeds DEFAULT_CONFIG from these values and then
applies URL parameters and stored Preferences, and the guarded update_config path
can move a paired device to another host in the same registrable domain. Effective
runtime destination has its own controls; this check does not cover it and must
not be cited as if it did.
The verifier reads these back OUT OF THE PACKAGED APK — from the
__VIZORA_RELEASE_ORIGINS__ marker the bundle stamps in at build time — and
refuses to publish on mismatch. Everything else in this file describes the
artifact's identity; this describes what it was built to point at, which nothing
checked until vizora-tv#18.
Why it was needed: until 1.3.13 the origins came from a gitignored, machine-local
.env, with a fallback to a DIFFERENT environment (api.vizora.io) when absent. An
APK aimed at the wrong backend has a valid package id, a correct version, the
right certificate and a perfectly good hash — it passed every check we had.
Must stay in lockstep with release-origins.json in the vizora-tv repo, which is
what the build compiles from. Changing one without the other fails the gate,
which is the intended behaviour: the two are a matched pair, and a mismatch means
the build and the publish disagree about where customers are being pointed.
The canonical Vizora Android customer-signing identity.
Every publish — INCLUDING THE FIRST — must produce an APK whose signing
certificate equals canonicalCertSha256. The `published` baseline below only
protects release 2 onward; pinning here is what protects release 1, which is
exactly where the 2026-08-10 mismatch was found.
Pin this ONLY after the key passes full durability verification: private-key
entry exists, certificate SHA-256 known, keystore has a secure off-machine
backup, credentials recoverable by an authorized operator, and restoration
tested well enough to prove the key still signs. Record classification and
ownership only — never a password or private-key material.
signing.backupClass: encrypted (aes-256-cbc/pbkdf2) copy on the company VPS at /opt/secure-backups/vizora/android-signing — dir 700, file 600, root-owned, outside every web, Docker and application root; credentials held separately in an owner-controlled password manager
_findings_2026_08_10: GATE B FAILED. The key that signed vizora-display-1.3.10-release.apk
(cert AA07524A…A5137982, created 2026-03-31) is NOT on the Windows build
machine. The only Android keystore there — vizora-tv android/vizora-release.jks,
single entry, alias vizora-display, created 2026-03-26 — carries a DIFFERENT
certificate: BE2320A5…3A9187A5. Not signed in CI, not the debug key, and no
other .jks/.keystore exists under the user profile or OneDrive.
DO NOT PUBLISH the existing 1.3.10 APK. Once canonicalCertSha256 is pinned to
a durable key, the verifier refuses that binary automatically — its cert will
_status_2026_08_10_evening: 1.3.11 has now been BUILT and fully verified against the on-machine key,
and its certificate is BE2320A5…3A9187A5 — matching the rehearsal candidate
exactly, which independently confirms which key actually signs here.
GATE B IS STILL FAILED, and it is the only thing between this build and
publication. Its two open items are facts about custody, not paperwork:
- no secure OFF-MACHINE backup of the keystore
- no credential recovery independent of this one Windows machine
Neither can be closed by an agent, because neither is a decision — they
require someone to actually place the backup and own the recovery.
Publishing before they are closed is the one irreversible move here: the
risk starts the moment a customer installs, and if the key is then lost
every TV in the field needs uninstall + re-pair to ever update again.
_playStoreNote: Before customer rollout, compare the canonical sideload certificate with the
Google Play App Signing certificate. If they differ, pilot customers migrating
from the sideloaded APK to the Play Store build will need one uninstall +
reinstall (and will re-pair). Document it before the migration, not after.

_comment: Built once from source 2026-08-13 on vizora-tv branch release/1.3.15, commit
8fb863cc09bcffafc45dec3bcf807707a6bf8579, tagged v1.3.15.
REPLACES THE REJECTED 1.3.14 CANDIDATE (see rejectedCandidates). 1.3.14 was verified
and Gate-A approved, then rejected by the operator on a defect found AFTER approval.
A new release identity was cut rather than rebuilding under the old one, so that the
v1.3.14 tag's statement about its commit and its bytes stays true.
DELTA vs 1.3.14: the entitlement invariant (vizora-tv#28, #31, fixed in #29) — once
tenant suspension is observed, no asynchronous renderer that began before it may
transition back to playing or place tenant content on glass. Two independent
instances (normal playlist prepare, temporary-content push), both reachable through
the ordinary billing dunning path, so both were live enforcement bypasses. The
playlist instance renders INDEFINITELY on the last item of a non-looping playlist,
because the illegitimate transition out of holding also cancels the self-heal retry.
Fixed via the engine's existing single supersession primitive rather than two
special-case checks, so a future asynchronous renderer is covered by construction.
69 insertions across src/main.ts and src/vizora-app.spec.ts, plus the version fields.
No dependency change, no android/ change beyond the version bump.
VERIFIED ON THESE EXACT BYTES, not inferred from the 1.3.14 run:
package / versionName / versionCode read from the binary manifest via aapt2
apksigner: verifies, v1+v2, single signer, all signers match the canonical cert pin
__VIZORA_RELEASE_ORIGINS__ extracted from inside the packaged APK and equal to the
releaseOrigins pin above
keepScreenOn + addFlags survive R8 in classes.dex, and a running install of THIS
APK reports fl=KEEP_SCREEN_ON in dumpsys window
replace-install over the LIVE published 1.3.13 bytes (downloaded from
vizora.cloud/downloads and hash-checked to C5C0B72C...F856C72): appId 10196
unchanged, firstInstallTime unchanged, and a file written before the upgrade
survived it. Paired screens keep their pairing.
Installs as an UPDATE over the published 1.3.13 — same certificate, versionCode
10145 > 10143. Do not uninstall first.

_comment: LIVE at https://vizora.cloud/tv and /downloads/vizora-display.apk since 2026-08-13.
Published bytes verified three ways, not asserted: by the publish path itself from the
server, by re-downloading the public URL independently afterwards (1250557 bytes,
sha256 identical), and on the server filesystem. The /tv page advertises the same
version and the same hash, because the page and the APK are uploaded as one operation.
compiledOrigins is populated for the FIRST time here. 1.3.13 and everything before it
predate the __VIZORA_RELEASE_ORIGINS__ marker, so the release-over-release origins
comparison reported SKIPPED on this publish. From the next release onward it is a real
check with this artifact as the baseline.
WHY 1.3.15 AND NOT 1.3.14. The 1.3.14 candidate was built, verified and Gate-A approved,
then REJECTED before publication on a defect found after approval — a reachable
billing/entitlement enforcement bypass where an asynchronous renderer started before
tenant:suspended could commit its frame over the suspension holding screen
(vizora-tv#28, #31). Rather than rebuild under the same identity and falsify what the
v1.3.14 tag says about its bytes, that candidate was retired intact — see
rejectedCandidates — and this replacement was cut as a new identity. The release
verifier now refuses the 1.3.14 bytes outright.
Installs as an UPDATE over 1.3.13 (same certificate, versionCode 10145 > 10143), so
paired screens keep their pairing. Confirmed on an Android emulator against the LIVE
published 1.3.13 bytes before publication, not inferred from the version rule: app data
survived, uid 10196 unchanged, firstInstallTime unchanged.
The outgoing 1.3.13 bytes were archived server-side as
vizora-display-1.3.13-release.apk during this publish, named after the OUTGOING build,
and re-hashed to C5C0B72C…F856C72 afterwards.
ACCEPTANCE STATUS — stated plainly because it is the thing most likely to be assumed.
Production-connected acceptance was NOT completed before publication. It was attempted
and blocked: this build machine has Norton HTTPS inspection re-signing all TLS, and the
release APK correctly refuses the MITM chain (CertPathValidatorException: Trust anchor
for certification path not found), so the emulator could not reach production at all.
Weakening the client to trust it was explicitly forbidden and was not done.
So the following remain RUNTIME-UNPROVEN for this artifact and are post-publication
confirmation items, per operator decision 2026-08-13:
- the entitlement fix that is the entire reason for this release, on a built APK
- heartbeat appVersion persistence (0 of 24 devices carry the key today)
- durable impression persistence (content_impressions has 0 rows lifetime)
- resolver-backed pull / realtime update / heartbeat reconcile against production
They are covered by deterministic regression tests with mutation controls, and by
source review, not by observed production behaviour. The first customer installation
is the acceptance test.
PHYSICAL_TV_SMOKE = DEFERRED_POST_RELEASE.
This block is the baseline the NEXT release is compared against: its signing certificate
must match, versionCode must be strictly greater than 10145, and from now on its
compiledOrigins must match too unless an approved originTransition says otherwise.
PREVIOUS: 1.3.13, versionCode 10143, apkSha256 C5C0B72C…F856C72, published 2026-08-13
from commit 9efd6ee.

approval._gateA: Artifact approval — confirm this exact APK is the intended client-pilot build, not merely the newest GitHub prerelease.
_gateA_scope: APPROVED 2026-08-13 for 1.3.15, bound to apkSha256
95D1BC01B47E20BD87456D62FF905512D6030AC829DAB72B17AE7F16C74E2383 and nothing else.
HOW THIS APPROVAL WAS GIVEN, recorded precisely because Gate A is an operator control
and the timing was unusual. The operator rejected the 1.3.14 candidate and directed
the replacement in one instruction, which included: 'build once / compute new
SHA/bytes/cert / create new candidate release metadata / bind a fresh Gate A approval
to the exact new APK / tag v1.3.15 on the exact build source commit'. So the approval
was authorised in advance of the bytes existing, and the SHA-256 above was filled in
mechanically from the single build that instruction called for. It was NOT inherited
from 1.3.14 — that approval was reset to null when 1.3.14 was retired, which is the
control working.
If the operator considers advance authorisation insufficient for Gate A, reset this
block to null and re-approve against the recorded hash. Nothing downstream has run:
publication is a separate, explicitly withheld decision and /tv still serves 1.3.13.
The current Vizora Android release process is not established as byte-reproducible:
we have never demonstrated that rebuilding a given commit yields an identical binary,
so a rebuild must be assumed to VOID this approval. Reset to null and re-approve if
that ever happens. This build was deliberately run ONCE for that reason.
WHAT THIS APPROVAL COVERS: the TV source merged to vizora-tv master, packaged
unchanged, plus the version bump. The delta from the rejected 1.3.14 candidate is the
entitlement-invariant fix (vizora-tv#29, closing #28 and #31) and its two
deterministic regression tests. Binary facts were verified mechanically on these exact
bytes before approval — package, versionName/versionCode, pinned certificate,
cross-scheme apksigner, compiled origins extracted from inside the APK, keep-screen-on
live in dumpsys, and a real replace-install over the LIVE published 1.3.13 bytes that
preserved app data and uid.
PHYSICAL ACCEPTANCE STILL OWED, and it is deliberately NOT waived. The paired-device
acceptance (tasks/gate2-paired-device-acceptance.md) has not been run against this
candidate. The operator's instruction is explicit that Gate 2 runs against the FINAL
1.3.15 candidate rather than the abandoned 1.3.14 one, and that the TV1/Lobby re-pair
is scarce evidence not to be spent validating an artifact already decided against.
So this approval covers the ARTIFACT's identity and integrity; it does not assert that
the paired-device loop has been observed on hardware. Do not publish before it has.
PRIOR APPROVAL, superseded: 1.3.14 was approved 2026-08-13 bound to apkSha256
before publication. Preserved verbatim in rejectedCandidates.
_artifactApprovedSha256_comment: Gate A's binding, machine-readable. The prose above has always said the approval is
bound to one exact SHA-256 and that a rebuild voids it — but nothing enforced that:
publish only checked artifactApprovedBy was non-null, so an approval recorded for one
binary would have waved through any other. The verifier now requires this to equal
BOTH candidate.apkSha256 and the SHA-256 of the APK actually passed to publish.
Reset to null and re-approve whenever a new artifact is built.
approval._gateB: Signing-key durability — confirm the release keystore has a secure off-machine backup and a recoverable password owned by an authorized operator. Record location CLASS and ownership only, never the key or password.
_gateB_evidence: CLOSED 2026-08-10 (second attempt). Split by who established what, so a future
reader knows which parts are machine-checked and which rest on the owner.
Machine-verified: the encrypted backup was created, uploaded, then RETRIEVED
FROM THE VPS and restored — decrypt produced a file byte-identical to the
original (DB5C23DD…654BC3), which opened as PrivateKeyEntry alias
vizora-display and signed a disposable APK that apksigner verified across
v1+v2+v3 with certificate BE2320A5…3A9187A5. Isolation verified, not assumed:
no nginx root/alias into /opt, no container mount, 4/4 HTTP probes 404. The
original keystore re-hashed unchanged and every temporary copy was shredded.
Ciphertext on the VPS: A666578E…98A725F3, 600, root-owned.
Owner-attested (not machine-checkable, by design): both secrets — the backup
encryption passphrase and the keystore password — were filed in an
owner-controlled password manager and read back before the staging folder was
deleted. Confirmed by Srini 2026-08-10; the deletion was independently
re-checked here and no stray copy remains on the build machine.
Recovery after a total build-machine loss: vault -> passphrase -> decrypt the
VPS copy -> vault -> keystore password -> open. No step depends on the Windows
machine, which is what this gate exists to guarantee.
PRIOR INCIDENT, kept deliberately: this gate was closed and reopened earlier
the same day because the first passphrase was lost, making the first ciphertext
permanently undecryptable. The key was never at risk. The cause was ordering —
the staging folder was deleted before read-back from the vault was confirmed.
Filing a secret is not the same as having it. Re-run the restore drill
periodically; key custody rots quietly and only surfaces when it is expensive.
STILL CLOSED for 1.3.13 (2026-08-13). Nothing about the key or its custody
changed: 1.3.13 is signed by the same certificate BE2320A5…3A9187A5, which the
release gate re-checked against the pin, and no backup location, credential owner
or recovery path moved since 2026-08-10. This gate is about the KEY, not the
artifact, so it does not need re-closing per release — only re-checking that the
key and custody state are unchanged, which they are. The restore drill above has
not been re-run since 2026-08-10 and is the item that will age.
approval.signingKeyLocationClass: encrypted copy on company VPS outside all web/app roots + credentials in an owner-controlled password manager
